description: An eight-bit elementary cellular automaton clocked one generation at a time, with a gate output for each bit and a CV output taken from the eight bits read as a number

params.text: Sets the rule number, 0 to 255, that turns each generation into the next one; it starts at 90
Sets the eight-bit number the run starts from, 0 to 255; it starts at 30, and moving it restarts the run
Sets one end of the range of scale steps the quantized CV output is drawn from, 0 to 28 steps up the scale
Sets the other end of the range of scale steps, 0 to 28, and may be set below the low knob without breaking the range
Chooses which of the eight bits drives the clock output and gates the CV output, 0 for the least significant bit and 7 for the most
Chooses the scale the quantized CV is snapped to: ionian, aeolian, dorian, phrygian, lydian, mixolydian, major pent, minor pent, shang, jiao, zhi, todi, purvi, marva, bhairav, ahirbhairav, chromatic
At thru the CV output takes a new value on every clock; at sel only on a clock where the chosen bit is high. The tooltip calls this Clock output mode, but the clock output is the same either way
Chooses what the CV output carries: at qnt a pitch snapped to the scale, at raw a plain voltage scaled to the span set on the menu; it comes up at qnt
Clears the run and works out the first generation from the seed again, which is one step on from the seed itself

inputs.text: Steps the automaton on to the next generation on each rising edge, reading high at 1V and low again at 0.1V
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the run is restarted only by the reset button beside it
Adds its voltage to the rule number, one step per volt, with the total clamped to 0 and 255; polyphonic channels are summed first
Adds its voltage to the seed number, one step per volt, with the total clamped to 0 and 255; polyphonic channels are summed first
Moves that end of the range, adding nothing at -10V and all 28 steps at 10V on top of the low knob, so a cable resting at 0V adds 14 by itself
Moves that end of the range, adding nothing at -10V and all 28 steps at 10V on top of the high knob, so a cable resting at 0V adds 14 by itself
Moves the scale choice, adding nothing at -10V and all sixteen places at 10V on top of the scale knob, so a cable resting at 0V steps it on by eight
Moves the chosen bit, adding nothing at -10V and all seven places at 10V on top of the bit knob, so a cable resting at 0V adds three and a half before the total is rounded down

outputs.text: Carries 10V while the clock input is high and its own bit of the current generation is 1, and 0V the rest of the time
The current generation read as a number and turned into a voltage: at qnt a pitch at 1V per octave with the bottom of the scale at C3, at raw the number spread across the span set on the menu
Carries 10V while the clock input is high and the bit named by the bit knob is 1, and 0V the rest of the time

notes: nothing moves until a clock is patched to clock; the automaton takes one generation per rising edge there, and every output holds 0V while that jack is low
the eight gate outputs run from bit 0 at the top to bit 7 at the bottom, bit 0 being the least significant bit of the eight-bit generation
a rule of 0, or a seed of 0, gives generations that are all zero, so the gate outputs and the clock output stay at 0V however fast the clock runs
the picture on the panel is worked out from the rule and the seed alone and shows 64 generations of the run at once; it is redrawn when either knob moves, not on each clock
the white lamp beside each gate output shows that bit of the current generation, and the green lamp shows which bit the bit knob has chosen
menu: Raw CV output range: +/- 10V, +/- 5V, +/- 3V, +/- 1V, 0V - 10V, 0V - 5V, 0V - 3V, 0V - 1V — sets the span the CV output covers at raw, and changes nothing at qnt
